rationale: The request asserts 'direct print to stdout', but wiki orientation shows a dedicated cli/renderer.py ('Response renderer for AI-Parrot CLI agent REPL') and a devloop/console.py with a Rich Live painter, while rich/prompt_toolkit/questionary are already declared dependencies. The premise must be verified before designing a refactor, and the devloop console is a likely in-repo homologation target.

queries.intent: Read the CLI entrypoint to confirm how 'parrot agent <id>' is wired and which command group owns it
Read agent_repl.py — the Click command behind 'parrot agent' — to see session bootstrap and output path
Read repl.py, the REPL engine, to determine whether output goes through print() or a renderer, and how prompt_toolkit is used
Read renderer.py to establish what rendering capability already exists and whether it uses Rich
Count and locate raw print() calls across the whole parrot/cli tree to quantify the stated problem
Inventory every existing Rich import across the workspace to map the current Rich footprint and conventions
Read the devloop console engine — the most advanced in-repo console — as the homologation reference for a refactor
List the devloop CLI package files to see the full set of console/renderer components already built there
Locate prompt_toolkit usage sites to know which prompt features (history, completion, key bindings) are already wired
Find questionary usage — the already-declared interactive-prompt library — since it overlaps InquirerPy's proposed role
Read the CLI dependency block in the core pyproject to confirm which TUI libraries are declared and under which extra
Read the prior console-cli-agents spec to recover the original design intent and avoid re-litigating settled decisions
Read the devloop-cli-console spec, which already solved the Rich-console problem for a sibling command
Find how streaming agent output reaches the terminal, the key constraint for any Live/markdown rendering approach
Locate HITL / confirmation / approval prompts in the CLI to scope the InquirerPy-vs-questionary decision
Check whether Textual appears anywhere in the workspace already (docs, specs, deps) before proposing it
Recent commit history on parrot/cli to learn what has changed lately and who owns it
Find existing tests for the CLI/REPL to know what a refactor must keep green
Read the agentd console proxy CLI, a second consumer of the REPL, to check refactor blast radius
Read the devloop run renderer (Rich Live envelope painter) as the concrete streaming-render pattern to reuse

expected_findings: Whether 'parrot agent' truly prints raw to stdout or already routes through cli/renderer.py
The exact Rich footprint already present and the conventions it establishes
Whether devloop/console.py is a reusable console engine or devloop-specific
The questionary-vs-InquirerPy overlap (questionary is already a declared dep)
The streaming constraint that decides inline-Rich vs full-screen Textual
Blast radius: agentd proxy and any CLI tests that a refactor must not break
